evals.prompt: We're doing a claim-evidence alignment pass on our TSE paper about self-admitted GenAI usage in GitHub projects (evals/papers/tse26-genai-usage.pdf). Pull out the narrow quantitative claims and the abstract and contribution statements they back up, so the team can check them against the replication package later.
evals.expected_output: claims.json and claims.md for tse26-genai-usage. Broad statements come from the abstract, the contribution list and the conclusion. Narrow claims cover the quantitative RQ1-RQ3 results, including the regression discontinuity results on code churn, and compound statements such as contribution 4 are split. Qualitative codes are not recorded as claims, and every quote is found on its page.
expectations: claims.json exists and cea_claims.py validate prints CEA_VALID
Every recorded quote is found on its stated page of the paper's text
Every selected claim has a selection reason that names the broad statement or contribution it supports
At least one rejected candidate is recorded, and every rejected candidate is a quoted statement with a page and a reason
No number that only describes the study, such as a sample size, corpus size, codebook size, or agreement score, is recorded as a claim
No purely qualitative finding or summary is recorded as a claim or a broad statement (rejected candidates do not count)
No note judges whether a claim is supported; notes state facts that can be confirmed in the paper
The dataset size of 1,292 GenAI mentions and the inter-rater agreement scores are recorded as rejected candidates with reasons
The broad statements include contribution 4 on code churn
The churn results are split into separate claims for the general effect on churn and for the stronger effect for generation tasks
The counts behind the RQ1 rankings, such as the 105 code generation instances or the 176 source-file mentions, are recorded as claims
A note records at least one place where the paper's text and Table 9 or Table 10 disagree

evals.prompt: extract the claims from tse26-ai-code-review.pdf in evals/papers. I need the key quantitative results, where exactly they are in the paper and why each one matters
evals.expected_output: claims.json and claims.md for tse26-ai-code-review. Narrow claims cover the adoption and usage of AI-based code review actions, the accuracy of the LLM-assisted framework against human annotations, and the factors that influence whether comments lead to code changes. Each claim has a selection reason, and every quote is found on its page.
expectations: claims.json exists and cea_claims.py validate prints CEA_VALID
Every recorded quote is found on its stated page of the paper's text
Every selected claim has a selection reason that names the broad statement or contribution it supports
At least one rejected candidate is recorded, and every rejected candidate is a quoted statement with a page and a reason
No number that only describes the study, such as a sample size, corpus size, codebook size, or agreement score, is recorded as a claim
No purely qualitative finding or summary is recorded as a claim or a broad statement (rejected candidates do not count)
No note judges whether a claim is supported; notes state facts that can be confirmed in the paper
The abstract sentence that gives 16 actions, more than 22,000 comments and 178 repositories is recorded as a rejected candidate with a reason
A claim reports the accuracy of the LLM-assisted framework against human annotations
Claims report the factor results for review granularity (file-level vs. hunk-level), for trigger mode, and for comment content (share of code or length)
The accuracy of the Random Forest model used to explain the factors is recorded as a rejected candidate, not as a claim
The RQ1 result that 82.6% of repositories customized a parameter is recorded as a claim whose `serves` list includes a broad statement stating that result
The claim on manually triggered comments gives its numbers or points in a note to where they are (Table XIII or the numbered sentence on page 11)

evals.prompt: Can you do the claim extraction step for the IEEE Software article evals/papers/ieeesw26-ai-slop.pdf? Record the claims with page numbers and also the ones you decided not to count.
evals.expected_output: claims.json and claims.md for ieeesw26-ai-slop, a qualitative study. Few or no narrow claims are selected. Counts that describe the corpus and codebook, such as 1,154 posts, 15 documents and 15 codes, are rejected candidates rather than claims, and the themes are not recorded.
expectations: claims.json exists and cea_claims.py validate prints CEA_VALID
Every recorded quote is found on its stated page of the paper's text
No narrow claim is selected, and the run's report or a note says why the paper has none
At least one rejected candidate is recorded, and every rejected candidate is a quoted statement with a page and a reason
No number that only describes the study, such as a sample size, corpus size, codebook size, or agreement score, is recorded as a claim
No purely qualitative finding or summary is recorded as a claim or a broad statement (rejected candidates do not count)
No note judges whether a claim is supported; notes state facts that can be confirmed in the paper
The corpus and codebook counts (15 documents, 1,154 posts, 15 codes) are recorded as rejected candidates with reasons
The coding counts on page 3 (such as 84.7% of posts coded or the three most frequent codes at 44.2% of codings) are recorded as rejected candidates with reasons, not as claims and not left out

Statements that give a frequency only in words, such as 'a dominant theme' or 'widely discussed', are not recorded at all, not even as rejected candidates (this includes word-only rankings such as 'pairs most often with')
The thematic clusters (Review Friction, Quality Degradation, Forces and Consequences) are not recorded as claims
